title: Third-party accelerator compatibility and dependency matrix (compatibility manifest)
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Summary:
This page is the canonical compatibility and dependency matrix for third-party accelerators that the runtime supports or plans to support. It codifies driver/runtime/library versions, expected kernel features, known incompatibilities, required CI smoke tests, ownership, and an automated manifest format (JSON) used by our onboarding toolchain. Use this when: planning support for a new accelerator, triaging inference regressions on a new hardware class, or validating release gates before a runtime rollout.

Goals:
- Capture the minimal set of platform packages (drivers, runtimes, libs) required for the serving runtime to deliver production SLOs.
- Provide reproducible test matrix entries used by CI and the hardware lab.
- Surface common failure modes and triage steps specific to each vendor.
- Define rollback and mitigation procedures when a hardware-specific kernel or driver causes regressions.

Scope and conventions:
- This document covers: NVIDIA (CUDA/NVML/NCCL), AMD (ROCm/MIOpen), AWS accelerators (Inferentia/Trainium), Intel/OneAPI-backed accelerators, Graphcore/Poplar, and other partner ASICs where we have lab access.
- Each matrix row includes: vendor, model family, required host kernel ABI, driver/runtime version range, critical libraries, recommended Docker base images, CI test IDs, owner, and known-risk flags.
- Version ranges are inclusive. Entries marked "experimental" must pass the experimental-canary CI suite, not just the smoke suite.

Compatibility matrix (text table):
Note: use this table as a quick reference. The source-of-truth is the JSON manifest in the repository at infra/accelerator-manifests/compatibility-manifest.json.

| Vendor | Family / Models | Host kernel ABI | Driver / Runtime | Critical libs / plugins | Recommended image tag | CI test(s) | Owner | Risk notes |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|-----------|-------|------------|
| NVIDIA | A100, H100 (Tensor) | linux-5.15+ (glibc ABI stable) | CUDA 12.2 - 12.4, NVIDIA driver 535+ | cuBLAS, cuDNN, NCCL, NVML | redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026 | ci-accel-nvidia-smoke, ci-nvlink-stress | runtime-hw | NVLink firmware mismatch causes memory teleport errors (see known issues) |
| AMD | MI250, MI300 | linux-5.15+ (ROCm-ready ABI) | ROCm 5.8 - 6.0 | MIOpen, ROCm NCCL-compatible libs | redwood/runtime-amd:rocm5.8-rt-2026 | ci-accel-amd-smoke, ci-rocm-memory-fft | runtime-hw | GPU page table fragmentation risk under high concurrency |
| AWS | Inferentia | linux-5.10+ (aws kernel) | Neuron SDK 2.3+ | neuron-libs, neuron-runtime | redwood/runtime-aws:neuron2.3-rt | ci-aws-inferentia-smoke | platform-partner | Binary ABI for Neuron is sensitive to compiler flags; require vendor-signed kernels |
| Intel | Gaudi/ Habana (Partner) | linux-5.15+ | Poplar / OneAPI stacks | poplar-rt, onednn | redwood/runtime-intel:oneapi-2026-rt | ci-intel-accel-smoke | runtime-hw | Driver installer writes kernel modules to non-standard paths; watch mknod/udev permissions |
| Graphcore | IPU-M2000 | linux-5.15+ | Poplar 2.x series | poplar-plugins | redwood/runtime-ipu:poplar2-rt | ci-ipu-smoke | runtime-hw | High cold-start memory usage; require warmup harness |

(For an up-to-date machine-readable matrix, see infra/accelerator-manifests/compatibility-manifest.json in the infra repo.)

Manifest format (example JSON snippet):
This is the canonical object the onboarding automation consumes. Store one file per vendor-family in infra/accelerator-manifests/.

{
  "vendor": "nvidia",
  "family": "h100",
  "models": ["h100-sxm", "h100-pcie"],
  "host_kernel_min": "5.15",
  "driver_version_range": "12.2:12.4",
  "required_packages": ["nvidia-driver>=535", "cuda-toolkit>=12.2", "libnccl>=2.15"],
  "recommended_image": "redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026",
  "ci_gate": "ci-accel-nvidia-smoke",
  "risk_flags": ["nvlink_firmware_sensitivity"]
}
(When editing the manifest, increment the manifest_version field and attach the matching lab test run id.)

CI and lab test design:
- Smoke suite (ci-*-smoke): quick boot, telemetry, single-request inference for canonical models, KV cache sanity, and basic memory pressure. Completes in < 5 minutes per node. Required for all PRs that touch runtime scheduler or kernel selection.
- Stress suite (ci-*-stress): multi-concurrency sustained runs, NVLink/PCIe saturation tests, rendezvous N random seeds to detect numerical drift. Runs in ~2 hours across our lab pool. Used for release gating on major driver bumps.
- Fidelity suite (ci-*-fidelity): compares output distributions against golden corpora, quantization toggles, and mixed-precision paths. Used when enabling quantization profiles.

CI matrix YAML example (used by our GitHub Actions):

name: Accelerator Compatibility Matrix
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  matrix-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        vendor: [nvidia, amd, aws]
        model_family: [h100, a100, mi300, inferentia]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Launch lab node (or mock)
        run: ./infra/labctl/launch_node --vendor ${{ matrix.vendor }} --family ${{ matrix.model_family }}
      - name: Run smoke tests
        run: ./infra/ci/run_compatibility_smoke.sh --manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/${{ matrix.vendor }}-${{ matrix.model_family }}.json

Known failure modes and triage playbook (quick reference):
1) Driver mismatch at startup (symptoms: driver load failures, NVML unavailable, crate reports "missing kernel symbols").
   - Commands: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv; rocminfo; sudo modinfo nvidia
   - If driver ABI mismatch: pin to the last known-good driver (see infra/accelerator-manifests/last-known-good) and trigger a canary rollout.
2) NVLink firmware mismatch (symptoms: inter-GPU copy hang, elevated kernel errors, OOMs during large KV cache warmups).
   - Triage: check nvidia-smi -q -d LINK; check firmware version table in infra/hardware-inventory/firmware.csv. If mismatch detected: set scheduling policy to avoid cross-socket NVLink paths (see mitigation below) and file an infra ticket for firmware alignment.
3) Host kernel OOPS when loading vendor kernel modules (symptoms: kernel oops, machine reboots, module load stacktrace).
   - Triage: capture vmcore if possible; collect /var/log/kern.log; isolate kernel version and report to partner. Revert kernel update and boot previous AMI.
4) Inference numerical drift after driver update (symptoms: fidelity alerts, increased model perplexity).
   - Triage: run ci-*-fidelity suite on the same commit+driver to confirm; if deterministic, mark driver as blocked for quantized paths and force fallback to float kernels; open follow-up with research and vendor.

Mitigations and operational knobs:
- Scheduler-level mitigation: 'evict-across-nvlink' boolean in scheduling profiles. When true, the scheduler will prefer cross-socket placement only for requests that are tagged as high-throughput and tolerant of additional latency.
- Kernel selection fallback: runtime keeps a per-node kernel-hint file produced by the onboarding manifest. If a kernel path is missing at startup, runtime will: 1) degrade to a compatible kernel plugin (if available), 2) reduce concurrency quota for the tenant, and 3) emit an operational alert with a suggested rollback.
- Container image pinning: all production pools use image digests (sha256) instead of tags. The manifest includes recommended image digests under recommended_image_digest.

Rollback and canary process for driver/runtime changes:
1) Staging validation: the proposed driver/runtime version must pass the smoke and stress suites in staging (staging-lab with 3 nodes) and not regress more than 1% on 95th p99 latency for canonical prompts.
2) Canary: roll to 5% of production traffic in a single region with canary telemetry enabled. Observe per-model fidelity metrics for 24 hours.
3) Rollback criteria: any of the following triggers a rollback: p99 latency increase >10% vs baseline, fidelity regression >0.5% for golden prompts, GPU hardware errors >0.1% of requests.
4) Rollback steps (operator):
   - Set scheduling policy to avoid affected pool(s): curl -X POST $RUNTIME_API/pools/scale -d '{"pool":"h100-rt-prod","target":0.9}'
   - Trigger node drain: infra/labctl/drain_node --node h100-rt-12
   - Re-image node with last-known-good driver image: infra/ami-bootstrap/reimage --ami ami-xyz --manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/last-known-good/nvidia-h100.json
   - Monitor: validate smoke-suite; close incident if green.

Ownership and contact matrix (text):
- runtime-hw (owner): Priya Nambiar, Luis Ortega — Responsible for manifests, smoke tests, and lab coordination.
- infra (owner): Jonah Park — Responsible for AMIs, kernel builds, and lab node boots.
- research/applied-ml: Maya Chen — Responsible for fidelity suite, golden corpora, and drift triage.
- platform-partner: Partner PM / Partner Eng — vendor-specific escalation.

Lab checklist before declaring full support:
1) Run full stress and fidelity suites for 48 hours across 3 nodes.
2) Validate billing/chargeback hooks for the pool (cost attribution).
3) Document warmup and eviction behaviors in the runtime pool README.
4) Add entries to hardware-inventory, include firmware and BIOS versions.

Operational examples and debug commands (cheat sheet):
- Check basic GPU health (NVIDIA): nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,LINK
- Check NVLink details: nvidia-smi -q -d LINK | egrep -A4 "Link"
- ROCm diagnostics: /opt/rocm/bin/rocminfo; /opt/rocm/bin/rocm-smi -d 0 --showtemp
- Container runtime test: docker run --rm --gpus all --privileged redwood/runtime-nvidia:cuda12.4-rt-2026 nvidia-smi -L
- Kernel module info: sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 40

Appendix A — Example compatibility test case (text):
- Test id: ci-accel-nvidia-smoke-001
- Purpose: Validate A100/H100 basic inference path and KV cache warmup under 8 concurrent workers.
- Steps:
  1) Boot node with manifest infra/accelerator-manifests/nvidia-h100.json
  2) Pull recommended image digest and run containerized test harness: infra/ci/harness/run_infer_test.sh --image sha256:abcd... --concurrency 8 --model gpt-redwood-small
  3) Assert: 95th latency < 200ms, memory growth < 2GB/worker after 30s warmup, no GPU driver errors in dmesg.

Appendix B — How to update this manifest:
1) Edit infra/accelerator-manifests/<vendor>-<family>.json and bump manifest_version.
2) Run ./infra/ci/run_compatibility_smoke.sh --manifest <path> locally against a mock node or in the lab.
3) Create a PR against infra with the manifest and the lab run id attached. Tag runtime-hw and infra teams as reviewers.
